title: APPROVAL OF REVOCABLE PERMIT NO. 25-22 BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES AND LOS ANGELES YACHT CLUB
text:
RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVAL OF REVOCABLE PERMIT NO. 25-22 BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES AND LOS ANGELES YACHT CLUB
Transmittal 1
Transmittal 2
Summary
: Staff requests approval of proposed Revocable Permit No. 25-22 (RP No. 25-22) with existing tenant, Los Angeles Yacht Club (LAYC) for nonexclusive use of a 2,000 square foot area referred as the “Long Dock” located in San Pedro. LAYC will use the Long Dock for: short-term berthing during regattas; passenger pickup and drop off; small watercraft launch and retrieval; sailing school berthing; and similar activities. This proposed action will advance the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department’s (Harbor Department) Strategic Plan objective 4, strong relationships with stakeholders, by providing dock space that will be dedicated to expanding recreational activities at the LA Waterfront. Under Permit No. 724, LAYC currently pays rent to the Harbor Department for the operation and maintenance of structures and facilities for a yacht club and small vessel dry storage area. Proposed RP No. 25-22 will provide LAYC temporary access to the Long Dock that is not expected to go beyond one year at which time a separate transaction will place the Long Dock under control of another party. In the interim it is valuable to the Harbor Department to activate operations of the Long Dock for continued logistics support related to ongoing sail training activities leading to the LA28 sailing events. It is recommended that LAYC not pay rent for the use of this 2,000 square foot premises based on LAYC improving access to the waterfront area, expanding recreational opportunities including supporting LA28 sail training activities and creating inclusive, welcoming spaces for all visitors.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is categorically exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article III Class 1(18)b of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) find that it is in the best interest of the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department to grant Revocable Permit No 25-22 at no rent to Los Angeles Yacht Club in exchange for providing significant public benefit, including providing community access and programming and operating the premises to promote aquatic events; 3) approve Revocable Permit No. 25-22 with Los Angeles Yacht Club; 4) authorize the Executive Director to execute and the Board Secretary to attest to Revocable Permit No. 25-22; and 5) adopt Resolution No. ______________.
Workforce & Government Affairs
summary: Gives the Los Angeles Yacht Club rent-free use of a 2,000 square foot dock called the Long Dock in San Pedro for up to about a year, for regatta berthing, passenger pickup and LA28 sail training.
